notes: Identity verified from the supplied document: title Superior facial emotion recognition in adolescents with anorexia nervosa – A replication study; Anca Sfärlea, Christina Buhl, Linda Lukas, Gerd Schulte‐Körne; DOI 10.1002/erv.3103; European Eating Disorders Review 2024, 32:943–951. This is a full primary brief report (abstract, methods, results, discussion, references), not an abstract-only parse. No PDF is assigned. The Supplement is referenced but is not contained in the supplied source. Description specifies reaction time but no ANOVA term. TASK, EMOTION, TASK × EMOTION and collectively reported GROUP effects are distinct candidates; p. 4 does not uniquely identify one. Repeated descriptions cannot be assigned by row order or requested metric. RT candidate tests: TASK F1,72=405.55, p<0.001, partial eta-squared=0.849; EMOTION F3.53,254.18=131.98, p<0.001, partial eta-squared=0.647; TASK × EMOTION F3.20,230.38=105.87, p<0.001, partial eta-squared=0.595; all GROUP main/interaction effects are reported only collectively as Fs<1, without exact Fs, p values or partial eta-squared. No test selected from these candidates. Candidate common main-report analytic sample: 33 AN + 41 HC = 74 adolescent participants in mutually exclusive included groups; not derived from degrees of freedom. Main report describes the mixed TASK × EMOTION × GROUP ANOVAs and no additional participant exclusions for those reported models. Eligibility excludes IQ <85, visual impairments, specified neurological/psychiatric disorders and substance abuse; HC excludes current/past mental disorders. Endnote 2 describes a separate sensitivity analysis excluding two AN participants above the 10th BMI percentile; this is not substituted for the main analysis. Model sample cannot be assigned to an unidentified row-specific test; retain only as a candidate. Misclassification model inclusion/exclusions cannot be verified without Supplement. Authors explicitly describe successful replication at whole-study level; reported_success preserves that narrative verdict only, not a claim of a uniquely identified row-specific test. The neutral description mentions major depression; the replication actually compares AN with HC, with depression sometimes comorbid within AN, not a separate major-depression group. No mapping is inferred from row order, original statistics or numeric agreement.
